# Chrono Trigger orchestra bridge

`chrono.js` validates the unmodified USA v1.0 ROM with both CRC32 and SHA-256, checks the exact displaced instructions and unused insertion space, then patches a new byte array in browser memory. The uploaded ROM is not in this repository. Optional 512-byte copier headers are removed before validation. Unknown, modified, translated or already patched ROMs are rejected before any mutation.

The original 64-byte observer at file offset `0x5F370` latches actual validated song requests at `Audio_StartSong` (`C7:0A39`). It restores the complete 16-bit accumulator and processor flags, replays the displaced five bytes and continues the original routine at `C7:0A3E`. It leaves X, Y, direct page and data bank alone. The insertion area is documented as unused by the MSU-1 research and checked as zero bytes in the exact supplied ROM. The hook catches expanded song aliases, normal field music, battle interrupts and resumes that reach this routine. It captures requests, not an acoustic analysis or a continuous report of SPC playback position.

The WRAM latch begins at `7E:1EE0`: byte 0 is song, byte 1 is a wrapping sequence counter, byte 2 is the original command, byte 3 is the original second argument, bytes 12 and 13 are the `43 57` signature. The game audio boot clears this page. `readCue(player)` performs one native memory read and returns null until the signature and command are valid. It does not infer a song from a transient SFX command. Polls can miss an entire very short intermediate cue, so this is not frame-exact musical synchronization.

With `muteMusic:true`, a separate two-byte edit at file `0x72D11` changes the song-volume multiplicand to zero in the SPC700 `Spc_WriteVoice` routine. The original comparison at `0x72CFF` sends sound-effect tracks around these instructions, directly to `0x72D14`; those paths and the sound-effect groups are unchanged. Music still loads, runs, occupies its normal voices, supplies its normal samples and reports normal event timing to the game. This avoids replacing songs with silence tracks, which would change synchronization and sample-bank behaviour. The patch is designed to preserve the game's SFX gain path; it does not separate environmental effects encoded as music-table tracks, and it does not prove every sound throughout a complete playthrough.

The music mute applies to the uploaded SPC driver. Save states can contain that driver's code, so restoring a state made with another audio patch can restore its different audio behaviour. In this build, orchestra-off means silence the external orchestra while retaining the game's effects; it is not an original-soundtrack switch. Restart an unpatched game for the original soundtrack.

All 83 original song IDs have deterministic editorial roles in `CUE_MAP`. These roles select our original performances; they are not a reproduction or orchestration of the game's original compositions. Most labels show numeric game cue IDs; the small named subset is documented in the sources. New performance tracks can be added to a role without changing the ROM observer.

Run `node game/chrono/test.mjs` for 782 synthetic/interpreter checks. Supply a private extracted `.sfc` path as the last argument for 796 checks including the actual ROM. Tests independently execute every instruction in the observer across all 256 initial flag values and sequence rollover; they check the caller stack and original continuation effects, checksum, no source mutation, header handling, revision rejection and the SFX branch. Full game completion and listening verification remain separate browser tests.

The module and observer are original integration code. References were used to identify and verify interfaces; no upstream patch implementation, ROM payload, soundtrack or full disassembly is redistributed here.
